candidates.name: rental_analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Self-described 'national, county-level rent-affordability dataset that refuses to lie about what it doesn't know, plus an agent that answers questions against it'. 979 KB repo, no committed language flag (mostly data), created 10 Sep 2026, pushed 13 Sep 2026 (very fresh, active). Likely built on HUD FMR / Census ACS given phrasing; exact source files not confirmed (page did not expose file tree to WebFetch).
candidates.why_useful: Directly targets gap 13 (long-term rental economics) with an explicit affordability/uncertainty framing; worth a manual clone-and-inspect given how recent and active it is.

candidates.name: Housing-Market-Data-Analysis (HUD API + Census Bureau)
candidates.what_it_holds: Jupyter notebook pipeline pulling HUD Fair Market Rent API data joined with Census ACS 5-year estimates into a county-level dataset covering all 50 states + territories; runs OLS in R on vacancy rate vs 2BR FMR. 51 KB, pushed 1 Jun 2026, no license.
candidates.why_useful: Working, current one-command-ish method to combine HUD FMR + Census ACS rent/vacancy at county grain nationally — directly reusable for a host-supply-economics panel (gap 13).
candidates.geography: US, all states + territories, county level

candidates.name: mcp-fairrent
candidates.what_it_holds: MCP (model context protocol) server exposing HUD housing data: Fair Market Rents and Section 8 income limits, as callable tools rather than a static dataset. Pushed 12 Sep 2026 (one day before this scout).
candidates.why_useful: A structured, queryable client for HUD FMR/income-limit data that an agent (or our pipeline) could call directly instead of hand-parsing HUD CSVs; very fresh.

candidates.name: fmr8-mcp-server
candidates.what_it_holds: Another MCP server, described as providing Section 8 Fair Market Rent lookups AND historical trends (implying some vintage/time-series access, not just current year). Pushed 20 Apr 2026.
candidates.why_useful: If the 'historical trends' claim holds, this is a rare pointer to point-in-time/historical HUD FMR access (relevant to gap 4's vintage-series ask), not just the latest cross-section.

candidates.name: hud (API Evangelist documentation)
candidates.what_it_holds: Documentation/catalog of the HUD public API surface, including Fair Market Rents and related datasets (income limits, etc.), pointing to HUD's own developer endpoints. Pushed 12 Sep 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Useful map of what HUD actually exposes via API (endpoints, coverage) to plan a direct pull rather than scraping — low novelty as data but saves discovery time.

candidates.name: fmr-map
candidates.what_it_holds: Interactive choropleth map of HUD Fair Market Rent by area; pushed 31 Aug 2026 (recent). Likely bundles a processed FMR-by-county/metro file to drive the map, though exact file format not confirmed.
candidates.why_useful: A recently maintained FMR visualization repo often carries a clean, joinable FMR-by-geography table as its data layer.

candidates.name: HudFmrDataAnalyzer
candidates.what_it_holds: Older (2014) Python tool for downloading/analyzing HUD Fair Market Rent data across years; 1 star. Could carry older vintage FMR files bundled from the mid-2010s.
candidates.why_useful: If it committed historical FMR files from ~2013-2014, that is a genuinely older vintage than what we currently hold; needs a file-tree check to confirm.

candidates.name: hud-fair-market-rents-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: An Apify actor (hosted scraper-as-a-service) for HUD Fair Market Rents, pushed 25 Jun 2026. No data committed to the repo itself; it's a scraper definition.
candidates.why_useful: One-command (Apify run) method to pull current HUD FMR tables if the official bulk download changes format; low value since HUD already publishes bulk CSVs directly.

candidates.name: redfin-market-pulse
candidates.what_it_holds: Automated ETL pipeline pulling U.S. real-estate market data from the Redfin Data Center (median sale price, inventory, etc. — Redfin's public bulk-download portal). Pushed 29 Apr 2026.
candidates.why_useful: A ready pipeline for Redfin's own public data-center CSVs (metro/county/zip weekly-monthly housing market stats) which sit adjacent to rent and are a supply-side signal for host economics.

candidates.name: Redfin-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Generic 'scrape housing market data' tool targeting Redfin; last updated Dec 2024, unclear which fields/geography it covers.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal — undocumented scope; only useful as a fallback method if redfin-market-pulse doesn't cover needed fields.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: redfin-market-pulse covers similar ground with clearer scope

candidates.name: mortgagerate-api
candidates.what_it_holds: Client/wrapper for retrieving current and historical US 30-year and 15-year fixed mortgage rates from Freddie Mac's Primary Mortgage Market Survey (weekly averages). Pushed 16 Jul 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Mortgage rates are a lever on host supply economics (buy-vs-rent-out decision, refinancing pressure on STR hosts) named explicitly in gap 13; this is a clean historical weekly series access method.

candidates.name: wa-housing-homelessness
candidates.what_it_holds: R analysis of rising rent costs vs homelessness in Washington State 2015-2024, built on Zillow ZORI and HUD Point-in-Time (PIT) homelessness counts. Pushed 17 Jul 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Rare multi-year (2015-2024) state-level panel combining ZORI with an independent HUD series; the underlying merged CSV, if committed, would be a decadal WA rent time series.

candidates.name: post_covid_rent_analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: County-level analysis of US rent trends before/after COVID-19 using Zillow ZORI data. Pushed 12 Jan 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Likely carries a committed county-level ZORI time series spanning pre/post-2020, useful as a ready county panel rather than re-downloading from Zillow directly.

candidates.name: Rental-Planner
candidates.what_it_holds: ML tool (XGBoost) predicting 12-month rent trends by ZIP code using Zillow ZORI data. Pushed 25 May 2026.
candidates.why_useful: ZIP-level ZORI granularity is finer than county; if the raw ZIP panel is committed it's a useful finer-grained rent series.

candidates.name: zillow_market_analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Clustering of housing markets based on Zillow's ZHVI (home value) and ZORI (rent) data, combining both series. Pushed 9 Dec 2024.
candidates.why_useful: Joint ZHVI+ZORI file, if committed, gives both price and rent series in one place for a market-clustering cut — modest incremental value over pulling Zillow's own CSVs.

candidates.name: US_Census_Building_Permits
candidates.what_it_holds: Web-scraped US Census Bureau building permits data with Python scripts producing Tableau visualizations. Last updated 2021.
candidates.why_useful: Building permits proxy new housing (and indirectly new STR-eligible) supply, named explicitly in gap 13; stale but shows the acquisition pattern for Census permit series.

candidates.name: bls-census-housing-analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: End-to-end pipeline ingesting BLS QCEW (employment) and Census building permits, normalizing into analytical views with reproducible metrics. Pushed 20 Mar 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Combines labor-market and permit data at a reproducible-pipeline level; permits piece overlaps gap 13 (housing supply) and could be adapted rather than built from scratch.

candidates.name: Housing_Affordability_Analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Analysis of rent-to-income affordability across US counties, evidently HUD-FMR-adjacent per its sibling repos from the same account family (e.g. Zoning-and-Rent-Burdens). Pushed 7 Jan 2026.
candidates.why_useful: County-level affordability ratio series, if committed as data, is a directly usable host/renter-economics cut.

candidates.name: Zoning-and-Rent-Burdens
candidates.what_it_holds: Analysis of how zoning regulations affect rent burdens, using HUD FMR data as the rent series. Pushed 20 Apr 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Links zoning/regulatory restrictiveness to rent burden — a possible proxy for STR-adjacent housing-supply constraint by metro, tangential to gap 13 and gap 12 (regulation).

candidates.name: MassachusettsRealEstateInvestmentAnalysis
candidates.what_it_holds: AWS cloud pipeline analyzing Massachusetts real estate using Zillow ZHVI & ZORI data with a Streamlit dashboard. Pushed 28 Apr 2026.
candidates.why_useful: State-scoped joint ZHVI/ZORI pull; narrow geography limits usefulness beyond a single-state cross-check.

notes:
MODALITY CONSTRAINT HIT: this session's WebSearch tool returned 'budget exhausted (200/200)' on the very first four queries, before any of my searches ran — evidently shared/consumed across other concurrent scout agents in this sweep. I pivoted to WebFetch against github.com's HTML search (got 429 rate-limited, Retry-After 3600, likely also hit by sibling scouts) and then to api.github.com/search/repositories via WebFetch, which mostly worked but intermittently 403'd (looks like the unauthenticated secondary rate limit, ~5-10 req/min) and recovered after spacing calls out. DuckDuckGo HTML hit a CAPTCHA wall; Bing HTML returned no github.com results for site: filtered queries (WebFetch's summarizer likely couldn't parse Bing's JS-rendered link structure). Net effect: coverage here is real but shallower than a full gh-CLI or open WebSearch pass would give — recommend a follow-up scout with gh CLI or fresh WebSearch budget on this same theme.

Substantive finding: there is no evidence of a genuine 'official' Zillow, Apartment List, Redfin, or Realtor.com GitHub org that publishes research-grade rent data as committed files or releases — Zillow's own GitHub org is pure engineering/YUI-framework tooling; Apartment List's org is internal dev tooling (style guides, pubsub wrappers) with no data repos; I found zero results for Realtor.com rental data repos and zero for a standalone Apartment List rent-report mirror. This roughly matches expectation: these vendors publish current bulk CSVs directly from their own websites (Zillow /research/data, Redfin's Data Center, HUD's own FMR bulk downloads), so GitHub's incremental value is almost entirely (a) small student/analyst repos that pulled a snapshot for a class project (rarely long historical, rarely well-documented, potential capped at low-medium), and (b) a handful of genuinely useful ACQUISITION METHODS: two MCP servers for HUD FMR (haksanlulz/mcp-fairrent, nikvb/fmr8-mcp-server — the latter claims historical trends, worth checking for point-in-time value against gap 4), a Freddie Mac mortgage-rate API client (apiverve/mortgagerate-api), and a Redfin Data Center ETL pipeline (dudubomb/redfin-market-pulse). The single most interesting hit, VikNim/rental_analysis, is worth a direct clone-and-inspect by a teammate with gh access — it's very fresh (created/pushed within the last few days of this scout), sized at ~1MB (too big to be just a README, too small to be a huge multi-year panel), and explicitly frames itself around a county-level rent-affordability dataset with calibrated uncertainty, which is unusual framing for a student project and could be either a genuinely careful build or another one-off. I could not get its file tree via WebFetch (GitHub's repo page didn't expose contents in the fetched summary) — that needs gh CLI or Read after a clone. None of the 20 candidates rate 'high' — nothing here is a substantial multi-year national panel beyond what Zillow/HUD/Redfin already give for free with one click, so the honest read is: for this theme, going directly to the vendors' own bulk-download pages is very likely still better than anything on GitHub, EXCEPT for point-in-time/vintage FMR access (nikvb/fmr8-mcp-server's 'historical trends' claim, unverified) which would be new if it holds up, since HUD's own site does not obviously expose FMR vintages the way ALFRED does for macro series.
